claims.text: TaVCrW is a disordered BCC solid solution at 0 K.
GGA-PBE/LDA underbinding or overbinding errors affect TaVCrW, particularly its V and Cr constituents, at 0 K.
Electronic-excitation effects in TaVCrW are negligible at low temperature.
An MTP trained on TaVCrW DFT data can replace the EAM reference potential in the melting calculation.
FEP can replace thermodynamic integration for calculating the TaVCrW solid-liquid free-energy difference.
A supercell containing more than approximately 100 atoms is sufficient to capture the relevant SRO correlations.
The proposed method is applicable over 2000-2400 K provided unmodeled magnetic fluctuations are not activated.
Solid-state SRO stabilizes TaVCrW by approximately 2-3 meV/atom.
Accurate reproduction of the ab initio phase-space distribution, including local environments and SRO, is critical to the validity of the FEP estimator.
The MTP provides a computationally efficient surrogate for the DFT energy landscape.
Using the MTP enables rapid phase-space sampling for FEP.
FEP obtains the solid-liquid free-energy difference by perturbing the system along a coupling parameter and thereby bypasses the slow convergence of thermodynamic integration.
The MTP preserves electronic-structure features such as a DOS gap that affect the melting point.
Empirical potentials commonly miss the relevant SRO and electronic-structure features.
MTP plus FEP will reduce computational cost by more than 80% relative to TOR-TILD.
The MTP plus FEP melting temperature will be within 10-20 K of the DFT-TOR-TILD baseline.
The FEP solid-liquid free-energy difference will deviate by less than 0.5 meV/atom from the thermodynamic-integration baseline.
High-temperature magnetic fluctuations may shift the TaVCrW melting point.
Errors in the underlying DFT functional may be inherited by the MTP and affect the absolute melting-point prediction.
A benchmark comparison against TOR-TILD can falsify the method by measuring free-energy error, melting-temperature deviation, computational cost, and SRO under matched supercell conditions.

contradictions.description: The intervention says FEP replaces thermodynamic integration, but the mechanism describes FEP as perturbing the system along a coupling parameter, which resembles the coupling-path procedure attributed to thermodynamic integration and leaves the methodological distinction internally unclear.

The hypothesis requires a cost reduction exceeding 80%, but the falsification rule does not reject the hypothesis for cost reduction below 80% unless the melting-temperature deviation also exceeds 20 K. Thus a direct failure of the stated cost requirement need not falsify the hypothesis.
